question_record.context: In a recent security incident, a known credential theft tool execution command line was detected indicating potential credential dumping. The process `mimikatz.exe` was executed, which might have been an attempt to dump users' credentials, keys, and plain-text passwords. This incident reported malicious activities from the actor Manatee Tempest, a Russia-based cybercriminal group active since June 2014. They are known for using malware campaigns such as the Dridex banking trojan and establish command-and-control channels for Cobalt Strike beacons through domain fronting.
question_record.question: Can you identify the URL associated with the activities of the Manatee Tempest group detected in this incident?
solution: A known credential theft tool was detected on the host with AadDeviceId `4d8d23e9-a77d-4e33-9435-b8c457e57ca1`.
Lateral movement to the jump server `Vnevado-jump` was conducted via IP `99.83.111.100`.
Suspicious remote activity was observed involving the user with AadUserId `731adb71-b11c-4bbf-850b-57989b350e96`.
Activity linked to the Manatee Tempest cybercriminal group was observed, with a URL potentially associated with the group: `vectorsandarrows.com`.

136.name: Manatee Tempest activity group
136.description:
The actor that Microsoft tracks as Manatee Tempest is a Russia-based cybercriminal group that has been active since June 2014. It was notorious for one of its earliest malware lexpaigns – the Dridex banking trojan. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

For more information, read the Actor Profile: Manatee Tempest Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/a22c3410-db8f-4c58-866e-ebb760e509d0/analystreport

steps.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT o.AlertId, o.AlertTitle, o.ObservedAt, o.EntityIndex,
       o.GraphValue AS value, o.RawComponents, o.Roles, o.SourceRowHash,
       i.GraphValue AS matched_input
FROM LTMInputEvidence i
JOIN LTMEntityEvidence o ON o.SourceRowHash = i.SourceRowHash
WHERE i.AlertTitle = %s
  AND i.Concept = 'Command_File_Mention' AND o.Concept = 'Device_AAD_ID'
  AND i.GraphValue IN (%s,%s,%s,%s)
ORDER BY o.AlertId, o.SourceRowHash, o.EntityIndex, o.GraphValue, i.GraphValue
LIMIT 501
